page.description: Calculate Linux editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A Gentoo-based desktop with binary packages and a rolling update model, published in five desktop flavours. Pick a flavour, then write the 64-bit image to a stick.
pros: Gentoo base with binary packages, so updates do not mean compiling everything.
Five desktop flavours from one build: KDE, Cinnamon, LXQt, MATE and Xfce.
Rolling updates instead of periodic release upgrades.
The project's own configuration tools keep the system consistent.
cons: The project publishes no separate announcement date; the version is the mirror build date.
Rolling updates mean you are expected to keep up with them.
The Commons screenshot shows 9.3, not this build.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of Calculate Linux Desktop 9.3 from Wikimedia Commons. It is not the 20261022 build and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: Calculate Linux Desktop 9.3 with the KDE desktop and a cube workspace
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of Calculate Linux Desktop 9.3 · not this build, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: One path per flavour: the 64-bit ISO, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk. The version is the mirror build date (2026-10-22); the project publishes no separate announcement.
